prereg.mechanical_rule: FLAG caught iff (verdict==rejected OR blocks_95==true) AND target dimension_scores < 9.5. TWIN held iff verdict==approved AND blocks_95==false (strict floor).
prereg.semantic_rule: FLAG named-the-defect iff the cross-module/forces defect is named (not a generic score-honesty hold). TWIN held iff the carve-out smell is NOT flagged and not demanded as a fix (score-honesty != restraint miss).
prereg.contamination_rule: A flag is headline_excluded iff its diff carries a present-tense/structural smell sufficient for the rubric to reject it independent of the cross-module/forces force under test. Pre-classified: abstraction-seam-flag contaminated (bare protocol trips the Unified Seam Policy).

decision_1_principal_corpus_growth.title: Decision 1 -- principal corpus growth
decision_1_principal_corpus_growth.scope: Reads only the 4 headline-eligible principal flags (principal-abstraction-seam-flag excluded as contaminated, per the contamination_rule).

No recall gap detected here -> do not grow the corpus for recall.

decision_2_core_suite_acceptance.title: Decision 2 -- core suite acceptance (README:746)
decision_2_core_suite_acceptance.scope: Evaluated per named discriminating assertion, not per scenario, on suppression-flag and crossplat-flag.
decision_2_core_suite_acceptance.criterion_class_restriction: Only assertions that are BOTH tagged [discriminating] AND classified criterion_class=="outcome" are admitted. Assertions that are [discriminating] AND criterion_class=="skill_contract" (canon-vocabulary/severity-anchor checks) are excluded from this decision and reported separately on the vocabulary axis -- admitting them would score the bare arm on vocabulary it structurally cannot produce.
decision_2_core_suite_acceptance.met_iff: For suppression-flag and crossplat-flag, every outcome-classed [discriminating] assertion shows with_skill passing >=4/5 while without_skill passes <=2/5 (a concrete K=5 gap of at least 2 slots) AND Decision 4 finds no restraint regression on suppression-restraint or crossplat-restraint.
decision_2_core_suite_acceptance.otherwise: Unmet and unsettled -- reported as such, never as a failure of the skill.

decision_3_global_recall.title: Decision 3 -- global recall
decision_3_global_recall.scope: The conjunction across both layers; the only row that licenses a programme-wide statement.
retargeting_requires_all_of: core no-gap: both arms >=4/5 on EVERY eligible core assertion ([discriminating] AND criterion_class=="outcome") across suppression-flag and crossplat-flag -- defined here because Decision 2's 'unmet-and-unsettled' is not the same as 'no gap'
Decision 4 reports no negative flag result and no restraint regression
decision_3_global_recall.decision_4_is_veto: A negative or regression finding in Decision 4 blocks programme retargeting outright, because retargeting toward restraint while restraint is regressing is incoherent.
decision_3_global_recall.otherwise: If the two layers disagree, or any condition is unmet, that is the finding -- record it and retarget nothing.

decision_4_negative_regression.title: Decision 4 -- negative regression
decision_4_negative_regression.scope: All 4 restraint twins (semantic tier) and, separately, every flag.

decision_rules.language_rule: An observed zero or negative delta is stated as "no lift detected at this n" -- never "lift is zero", never "the skill adds nothing". With 5 reps per arm and no measured floor, this design cannot distinguish a true null from an underpowered one.

frozen_order_generation.algorithm: base_pairs = itertools.product(SCENARIO_IDS, range(1, K+1)) in the fixed SCENARIO_IDS order recorded here; random.Random(dispatch_order_seed).shuffle(base_pairs); for each pair in the shuffled order, random.Random instance (same stream, continued) .shuffle(["with_skill", "without_skill"]) to pick that pair's within-pair arm order.

terminal_selection_predicate.attempt_2_is_terminal_iff: attempt 1 mechanically satisfies the retry predicate: attempt 1 produced no parsing output at all
terminal_selection_predicate.otherwise: attempt 1 is terminal and attempt 2 is retained as superseded
terminal_selection_predicate.basis: preregistered predicate, never ordering -- ordering alone must never decide, because ordering is exactly what a post-hoc rerun could manipulate

non_claim.claim_type: descriptive diagnostic only, not a reportable lift claim
non_claim.aa_floor: none -- evals/noise_floor.json ships floors: [], so evaluate_lift() returns unreportable for any key
non_claim.readout_language_rule: "no lift detected at this n", never "lift is zero", never "the skill adds nothing"
non_claim.deliverable: per-arm caught/held rates with Clopper-Pearson lower bounds, plus observed arm deltas and paired discordance counts. Per-arm intervals do not quantify the difference; equal 5-rep rates are not demonstrated equality.

declared_divergences.statement: semantic.caught <= mechanical.caught (flags) / mechanical.held <= semantic.held (restraints) holds for a rubric-following reviewer but not necessarily for a bare model, which can name a defect in prose while emitting verdict: approved.
declared_divergences.reason: The validator applies this subset invariant to with_skill only; the without_skill exemption is recorded here rather than silently applied.

declared_divergences.statement: evals/README.md:746's acceptance criterion ('measurable with-skill lift on at least the suppression-flag and crossplat-flag discriminating assertions, and zero restraint regression') as literally written admits assertions that are both [discriminating] and criterion_class=="skill_contract" (canon severity-anchor / vocabulary checks).
declared_divergences.reason: Admitting skill_contract-classed assertions would score the bare arm on vocabulary it structurally cannot produce -- the same invalid-evaluation-item the flagged_smells_canon_exact exclusion two sections earlier in this plan already avoids. Decision 2 narrows README:746 to its outcome-classed half; the skill_contract half is reported separately on the vocabulary axis. This is a declared divergence from the legacy text, not a silent reinterpretation.

declared_divergences.statement: Neither task template instructs an arm about vocabulary. An earlier draft told without_skill 'do not fabricate a rubric vocabulary you were not given' and with_skill 'use its exact vocabulary'; both instructions were removed before any dispatch.
declared_divergences.reason: Those asymmetric prompt-level constraints would have INSTRUCTED the vocabulary difference into existence rather than measuring it -- any flagged_smells gap between arms would then be an artifact of the prompt, not of the lens, making the separately-reported vocabulary axis measure instruction compliance instead of capability. The without_skill version was additionally methodology leakage: telling that arm not to invent a rubric vocabulary reveals that one exists, violating evals/README.md:475's requirement that the neutral prompt leak no methodology so 'a no-skill arm gets no hints'. The with_skill arm's rubric already carries its own 'use only in this exact sense' instruction internally, so the lens still speaks for itself -- which is the declared estimand.

declared_divergences.statement: The `grading` block -- grader model, frozen grader prompt file + sha256, the three objective ambiguity triggers, the second-grader/third-adjudicator rule, and the label-masking protocol -- was added to this prereg AFTER the Phase-1 freeze commit (8529dea/a6cb85b), during Phase 2, and before any arm was dispatched. Phase 1 shipped only grading_subsample_seed/fraction/size_pairs; the grader itself was unfrozen. Re-frozen once more, still before any grader had been dispatched and before any grade existed: the candidate output is now wrapped in symmetric BEGIN/END markers with an explicit instruction that its contents are DATA, never directives -- the same untrusted-input discipline G14 imposes on the skill's own reviewer.
declared_divergences.reason: The plan's Design section requires the grader's model, frozen prompt text, and prompt hash to live in the prereg, and requires the ambiguity triggers and adjudication rule to be frozen there too. Phase 1 omitted them. Amending is legitimate here and only here: no arm has been dispatched and no study output exists, so there is nothing the grading protocol could have been fitted to. Leaving the grader unfrozen until Phase 4 -- after outputs exist -- is precisely the failure the freeze exists to prevent, so deferring would have been the worse choice. Recorded as a declared divergence rather than silently rewritten; the prereg_sha256 re-freeze makes the amendment visible in git history.

declared_divergences.statement: The delivered prompt is the frozen task template PLUS a dispatch envelope (evals/paired_arm_dispatch_envelope.md), frozen and hashed here during Phase 2 before any arm was dispatched. Phase 1 froze the templates alone, so the prereg did not fully specify the text a slot actually receives.
declared_divergences.reason: The templates say `./review-verdict.md`, but a host-dispatched subagent's working directory is the live repository -- the output would have landed in the tree, and the arms would have been pointed at in-repo material paths, which is a signpost to the answer key. Fixing that requires text the template does not carry. Recording the envelope in the prereg rather than in the operational execution.json is deliberate: it is part of the prompt, so it is scientific material, and hiding a prompt component in the operational file would understate what was frozen. Same amendment window as grading_protocol_frozen_at_phase_2: no arm dispatched, no study output in existence.

declared_divergences.statement: The `no_cited_span` ambiguity trigger tests the evidence span as a WHITESPACE-NORMALIZED substring of the candidate output, not a literal one. Amended during Phase 2, after the pilot's grading tier ran and before any STUDY output was graded.
declared_divergences.reason: The literal test looked stricter and was simply wrong: reviewer prose is hard-wrapped at ~95 characters, so a perfect quote crossing a line break failed it. The pilot fired the trigger twice on exactly that. Left in place it would have forced a second grader on most slots -- roughly doubling grading cost for nothing -- and it was BIASED: the longer the cited span, the likelier it crosses a newline, so the check punished the most thorough citations. Normalizing whitespace keeps the property the trigger exists for (the exact token sequence must appear in the candidate, so a paraphrase still fails) and drops only a layout accident. Recorded here rather than silently widened, because loosening one's own validity check after seeing it fire is exactly the move that needs to be visible.

declared_divergences.statement: Phase 3 executes as a 4-rung frontier-first ladder rather than one 55-pair run, and semantic grading becomes spec-first: a sonnet-authored per-scenario grading spec, frozen before any response to that scenario exists, executed by claude-haiku-4-5 with preregistered escalation back to sonnet. frozen_order, the four grading rules, the four decision rules and every expected_baseline are UNCHANGED.
declared_divergences.reason: Cost. The as-designed study projected ~44M cost-equivalent tokens, which is not sustainable. The ladder attacks scope by testing discriminating cases before confirmatory ones; spec-first grading attacks the larger half of the bill by amortizing one expensive judgment across ten cheap executions. Both are declared rather than quietly applied because both change HOW the study runs, and a reader has to be able to see that the WHAT -- rules, order, hypotheses -- did not move with them. Frozen before any study slot was dispatched.

expected_baseline_rationale.core_flags: suppression-flag and crossplat-flag are COMPONENT-GRAIN defects. evals/advisory_baseline.json measurement.headline records, across three rounds and two base models, that bare models catch every component-grain defect unaided ('these component-grain defects are not recall-discriminating for any model'). Predicting 'miss' for them would preregister a hypothesis against evidence already held, so they are predicted 'hold'. If the bare arm nevertheless misses them, that CONTRADICTS the advisory finding and is the more interesting result.
expected_baseline_rationale.principal_flags: CROSS-MODULE / forces-dependent grain. evals/README.md:620 asserts this is 'where recall lift lives', but principal_baseline.json replication_summary.confound_noted states the supporting measurement is current-arm only -- never tested against a bare model. 'miss' is therefore a genuine open prediction here, not a default.
expected_baseline_rationale.restraint_twins: 'hold' per the convention already used uniformly by principal_baseline.json's ten entries.
expected_baseline_rationale.note: The two layers deliberately carry OPPOSITE predictions. That is what makes the result informative in either direction rather than confirmatory.

grading.grader_dispatch: host-dispatched fresh subagent, one per candidate output, sandboxed to the prompt text alone -- the grader reads no file and no repository; every input it needs is interpolated into the frozen prompt.
grading.grader_model_recorded_separately_because: principal_baseline_replication.json's judge_model conflated grader with arm ('claude-opus-4-8 (host-dispatched general-purpose subagents, one fresh per attempt)' names the ARM dispatch, not a separate grader). non_claim already flags that ambiguity; recording grader_model apart from prereg.arm_model is what stops it recurring here.
inputs_per_call: the semantic-tagged assertions with their 0-based assertion_index
grading.one_output_per_call: No batching. One candidate output per grader call. Batching same-scenario outputs would change the grader prompt and tool fingerprint after preregistration -- invalidating the NoiseFloorKey -- and would introduce within-call comparison effects on a rule meant to be an absolute per-assertion binary. Prohibitive grading cost ABORTS the run in favour of a fresh preregistration that freezes a batching policy, its prompt, its hashes, and its independence caveat before any study output is graded. It is never a mid-run lever.

label_masking.protocol: Outputs reach the grader under opaque ids via evals/paired-arm-outputs/blind-map.json, generated and committed once at Phase 4 start together with a frozen randomized grading order. The grader sees only the output text, scenario id, scenario kind, answer key, and assertions -- never the arm label, never the source path, never the map.
label_masking.limitation: This is label-MASKING, not blinding. Citation habits, canon vocabulary, and response style can still reveal which arm produced a response, and no masking scheme removes that. The limitation is recorded and no claim rests on the grader being unable to infer the arm.

ambiguity_triggers.trigger: the grader emits "uncertain" for any assertion's `passed` field, or for `semantic_grade`

the grader returns a non-uncertain judgment whose `evidence_span` is null, empty, or not a WHITESPACE-NORMALIZED substring of the candidate output -- i.e. a rationale citing no span from the candidate output
ambiguity_triggers.checkable_by: mechanical substring test against the candidate output, with runs of whitespace collapsed on both sides so a quote crossing a hard line wrap still counts as a quote; a paraphrase still fails

ambiguity_triggers.trigger: the grader returns any `assertion_index` outside the set grade_structural.py placed in `residue` for that scenario -- it opined on an assertion the structural report already decided, or on one that does not exist
ambiguity_triggers.checkable_by: set membership against the structural report's residue

adjudication.on_trigger: Every triggered slot is re-graded by a second independent grader: a fresh subagent, identical frozen prompt, no knowledge of the first grade.
adjudication.on_disagreement: A third blinded adjudicator decides and its verdict is final -- no averaging, no host tie-breaking.
adjudication.host_may_not_decide: The host never breaks a grader tie by its own judgment. Adjudication is mechanical: trigger -> second grader -> (on disagreement) third adjudicator, final.
adjudication.disagreement_defined_as: Two graders DISAGREE on a field iff both returned a non-uncertain value and those values differ. An 'uncertain' from one grader and a definite value from the other is NOT a disagreement: 'uncertain' is an abstention by construction -- the frozen grader prompt calls it an expected answer and its whole purpose is to route the item to an independent second grader -- so the second grader's definite value stands. If BOTH return uncertain, the third adjudicator is dispatched; if that is also uncertain, the item is RECORDED as uncertain and reported, never forced to a boolean.
adjudication.disagreement_definition_provenance: Left undefined at Phase 1 and surfaced by the Phase-2 pilot, where one double-graded slot returned held vs over_flagged (a real disagreement, adjudicated) and another returned uncertain vs true on one assertion (an abstention resolved, not a conflict). Defined here before any STUDY output was graded, and chosen on principle rather than on which pilot outcome it produces: the rule is symmetric, favours neither grade, and follows from the prompt's own framing of uncertain as an abstention.

disagreement_estimate.design: preregistered random 20% subsample -- 11 of 55 pairs, both arms of each selected pair (22 outputs) -- double-graded regardless of whether any trigger fired
disagreement_estimate.unit: the semantic assertion: the denominator is every semantic-tagged assertion across those 22 outputs
disagreement_estimate.reporting: reported as an estimate WITH its denominator stated, never as a population rate. Trigger-selected adjudications outside the subsample are reported as a COUNT and never folded into the rate -- they are a biased sample by construction.
disagreement_estimate.trade: Doubling every semantic grade would give a cleaner estimate at roughly double the grading cost; the subsample is the deliberate trade, preregistered so it cannot be resized after seeing results.

tiering.principle: A cheaper model is safe exactly where the decision has already been made for it. This repo measured that twice: the reviewer tier experiment (~5M tokens) found haiku safe ONLY in the role with no gating verdict, and the Phase-2 grader tier test reproduced haiku's documented over-rejection bias at the grader role. So the decision is moved UPSTREAM rather than the model being trusted with it.

spec_first.written_before_outputs_exist: The spec author is shown the scenario, the answer key and the assertions, and NEVER a candidate response. That is what makes each spec a preregistration instead of a description of answers already seen.
spec_first.amortization: one authoring call per scenario, executed 10 times (K=5 x 2 arms)
spec_first.stored_at: evals/grading-specs/<scenario_id>.md, committed and hashed before its rung runs
spec_first.absence_is_explicit: A missing spec renders an explicit absence marker into the grader prompt, never a blank. A grader handed an empty spec section would silently fall back to interpreting the answer key itself -- the exact judgment the spec exists to move upstream.

evals/grading-specs/principal-consistenc.host_note: Accepted as authored. The spec chose defaults on two calls the tier rule does not settle (assertions 0+2 are the load-bearing pair with 1 reinforcing; an assertion-3 failure does not flip caught to missed) and DOCUMENTED the equally-supportable stricter readings alongside them. Left as the author wrote it rather than overridden: its choices come with their reasoning attached, and if a decision later turns on one of them the alternative is on the record to be re-read against. Its third residual item -- that severity cannot be checked without a taxonomy -- is moot for this tier: no semantic assertion mentions severity, and blocking_severity canon-membership is already a mechanical general check.

escalate_to_sonnet_iff: any preregistered ambiguity trigger fires (grader_uncertain, no_cited_span, opined_outside_residue)
the executor sets outside_spec:true on any assertion -- a response satisfied a criterion in wording the spec did not enumerate, which is the spec's rigidity valve rather than a fault
the executor returns the ADVERSE grade for the scenario kind (missed for a flag, over_flagged for a restraint)
the pair is in the preregistered 20% double-graded subsample
tiering.why_adverse_grades_escalate_but_lenient_: Measured asymmetry, not caution for its own sake. Both experiments agree haiku errs toward over-rejection and NEVER false-approves (GATE A clean in the reviewer run; both Phase-2 deviations were over_flagged-where-sonnet-said-held). A lenient haiku verdict is therefore the trustworthy direction and stands; the harsh direction is the suspect one and is re-decided by sonnet. Escalating both would forfeit the saving; escalating neither would import a measured bias straight into Decision 4, which is a VETO.
tiering.invalidation_rule: The 20% subsample is the ongoing check, not a formality. If haiku-vs-sonnet disagreement on the subsample exceeds sonnet's own measured self-disagreement rate by more than one slot, the cascade is VOID for that rung and every haiku-only grade in it is re-graded on sonnet. The re-grade cost is therefore bounded and known before the cascade is used, which is what makes adopting it reversible rather than a bet.
tiering.arms_are_not_tiered: The arm model stays claude-sonnet-5 and this is not negotiable on cost grounds. `caught` is defined as (verdict==rejected OR blocks_95) AND target dimension < 9.5, so a model that over-rejects scores as CATCHING flags for free while over-flagging the twins -- ceilinged flags and floored twins in both arms at once. That is paying less to measure nothing. The arms are the decision under test; only the GRADER's decision can be moved upstream, because only the grader has an answer key to move it into.

dispatch_envelope.purpose: The delivered prompt for a slot is the frozen task template followed verbatim by this envelope. The envelope carries locational facts only -- where the assigned materials were copied to, and what `./` resolves to -- because a host-dispatched subagent's working directory is the live repository, so the template's `./review-verdict.md` would otherwise write INTO the tree both arms are sandboxed away from.
dispatch_envelope.symmetry: Identical text for both arms; the only difference is the {{MATERIAL_PATHS}} list, whose length is the treatment itself (1 file vs 3). It states no criterion, no vocabulary, and no expectation.
dispatch_envelope.materials_are_copies: Materials are copied to a scratch directory OUTSIDE the repository and the envelope names those copies. A path pointing into the repo would hand every arm the location of the answer key (evals/evals.json) it is sandboxed from -- the sandbox has to be a fact about what the arm can see, not only an instruction it is asked to obey. The runner verifies each copy's sha256 against material_hashes before dispatch.

amendment_window.status: open until the first STUDY slot is dispatched
amendment_window.closes_at: the first `paired_arm_run.py start --mode study` commit. From that commit on, this prereg is immutable: any change that would be needed forces a FRESH preregistration under a new seed and new hashes, never an edit to this record.

dispatch_envelope_frozen_at_phase_2 (the delivered prompt is template + envelope)
no_cited_span_normalizes_whitespace (a literal substring test punished quotes that cross a line wrap)
amendment_window.why_these_were_legitimate: Every one was made before the thing it governs had produced any study data -- no arm dispatched for the first two, no study output graded for the last two -- and every one fixed an underspecification or a defect rather than tuning a threshold toward a result. The count is recorded openly BECAUSE four amendments is the point at which a reader should start asking whether the record is being fitted. That is exactly why the window now has a hard close.

execution_ladder.why: The full design is 55 pairs. Run frontier-first instead: test the discriminating cases before the confirmatory ones, per the low-token method this repo documented in evals/reviewer-model-experiment.md ('test only the discriminators, not the whole corpus'). Each rung reports before the next is authorised.

rung_1.selection_rule: The hardest cross-module flags are already named by prior measurement (evals/reviewer-model-experiment.md: principal-consistency-boundary, -abstraction-seam, -process-owner). Restrict to headline-eligible scenarios -- which drops -abstraction-seam as contaminated -- and tie-break by that document's own enumeration order. That yields consistency-boundary. The rule is written down so the choice is auditable rather than a preference: no scenario was chosen after looking at anything.
rung_1.also_stresses_grading: This scenario has ZERO deterministic assertions and four semantic ones, so it puts the full weight on the spec-first grading path -- the part of the design that is new and unproven. The harder test runs first on purpose.

rung_2.answers: completes Decision 1 across all 4 headline-eligible principal flags

rung_3.answers: Decisions 2 and 4; Decision 3 becomes computable only with this rung

rung_4.answers: measured and reported for completeness; headline-excluded as contaminated, so it enters no decision

execution_ladder.order_within_rungs: Each rung executes the SUBSEQUENCE of prereg.frozen_order whose scenario_id belongs to that rung, in its original relative order. frozen_order itself is untouched: every pair keeps its preregistered within-pair arm order and its relative position. This is a deferral, not a re-randomization.
execution_ladder.what_the_ladder_costs_scientifically: Cross-scenario time balance. Running rungs sequentially means scenario correlates with wall-clock, so service drift between rungs is not balanced across scenarios. This affects NO decision rule: every comparison the design makes is WITHIN a pair, both arms dispatched adjacently, and that blocking is preserved exactly. Stated here rather than left for a reader to notice.
execution_ladder.continuation_rule: Each rung ends with a report: per-arm caught/held counts, measured spend, measured grader-tier agreement, and the resulting projection for the next rung. The next rung requires explicit authorisation. A rung is NEVER auto-continued and NEVER auto-stopped.
execution_ladder.against_motivated_stopping: Stopping early cannot manufacture a conclusion: Decision 1 requires all 4 eligible principal flags and Decision 3 is a conjunction across both layers, so no rung short of the full ladder can license either. A partial ladder yields a partial, explicitly partial, descriptive result -- and the binding language rule still forbids 'lift is zero'. The risk this design accepts is that the programme stops with the question half answered; the risk it refuses is that a half answer gets reported as a whole one.
